The humanized TG Bama pig model provides a clinically relevant large-animal platform for investigating the pathophysiology of metabolic disorder-associated colonic diseases and may facilitate the development and preclinical evaluation of therapeutic strategies targeting intestinal dysfunction.

title: Inhaled biologics: A paradigm shift in drug delivery for proteins, vaccines, and gene-based therapeutics.
authors: Chamiyal, Aditya; Bonde, Smita
abstract: Pulmonary drug delivery has emerged as a promising platform for the administration of biologics, offering direct access to the respiratory tract while minimising systemic exposure and associated adverse effects. Recent advances in inhalation technologies, formulation engineering, and carrier systems have significantly expanded the scope of inhaled biologics beyond conventional therapies. This review provides a comprehensive overview of emerging inhaled biologics, including proteins, peptides, monoclonal antibodies, gene therapies, mRNA therapeutics, siRNA, CRISPR-based systems, vaccines, and nanocarrier-enabled delivery platforms. Key physiological barriers to pulmonary delivery, such as mucociliary clearance, alveolar macrophage uptake, mucus penetration, and epithelial transport, are critically discussed along with contemporary strategies to overcome these challenges. Recent developments in lipid nanoparticles, polymeric nanoparticles, liposomes, exosomes, and inhalable dry powder systems are highlighted for their role in enhancing stability, targeting efficiency, and therapeutic outcomes. The review also examines clinical translation, regulatory considerations, aerosol performance, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic relationships, and the integration of artificial intelligence in formulation design and precision delivery. Marketed inhaled biologics remain limited to a few products, including inhaled insulin. In contrast, most inhaled monoclonal antibodies, gene-based therapies, gene-editing approaches, and pulmonary vaccine platforms remain investigational, with evidence derived primarily from clinical studies at different stages or from preclinical models. This review distinguishes marketed products from clinical-stage candidates and preclinical proof-of-concept studies to clarify the current state of pulmonary biologic delivery.

title: Autocatalytic split-crRNA Cas12a circuit coupled with phosphorothioate G-quadruplex fluorescence for ultrasensitive ctDNA analysis.
authors: Wei, Jiaye; Tian, Yi; Song, Lianxiang; Li, Qiong; Liu, Qin; Ding, Xiaoping; Shi, Kai
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as an important biomarker for early cancer diagnosis and therapeutic monitoring; however, the ultrasensitive detection of low-abundance single-nucleotide variations (SNVs) remains highly challenging. Herein, we developed an autocatalytic split-crRNA Cas12a fluorescence platform, termed AutoSCas, for highly sensitive detection of EGFR L858R mutant ctDNA. Upon recognition of trace EGFR L858R ctDNA, activated split-crRNA Cas12a (SCas12a) cleaved the loop region of a cascade hairpin probe, resulting in the release of functional spacer RNA (sRNA) molecules. The liberated sRNA further activated additional SCas12a complexes in the presence of assistant DNA, thereby establishing a positive-feedback autocatalytic nucleic acid circuit for exponential-like signal amplification. Simultaneously, a phosphorothioate-modified G-quadruplex hairpin probe was introduced as a low-background "signal-on" fluorescence reporter. Activated SCas12a continuously cleaved the loop region of the probe, releasing phosphorothioate-modified G-quadruplex that subsequently bound Thioflavin T to generate strong fluorescence signals. Benefiting from the synergistic integration of autocatalytic amplification and low-background signals, AutoSCas achieved ultrasensitive and highly specific ctDNA detection with a detection limit as low as 2 aM. Therefore, AutoSCas platform provides a pre-amplification-free strategy for highly sensitive SNV analysis and expands the design of split-crRNA-based CRISPR sensing systems.

title: Comparative genomics of canine Leptospira interrogans ST17 strains reveals conserved gene content across heterogeneous clinical presentations.
authors: Turlande, Emilia; Paz, Lucas Nogueira; Viana, Marcus Vinicius Canario; Brenig, Bertram; Azevedo, Vasco; Pinna, Melissa Hanzen
abstract: Leptospira interrogans causes infections ranging from asymptomatic renal carriage to fatal acute disease. Whether this phenotypic variation is encoded in genomic content remains unresolved, and autochthonous strains from natural infections are underrepresented in comparative datasets. Eight Leptospira stains from naturally infected dogs in an endemic Brazilian setting were characterized by whole-genome sequencing, taxonomic assignment, MLST, persistent-genome phylogenomic, pangenome reconstruction, virulome profiling, CRISPR-Cas typing, characterization of cyclic di-GMP signaling proteins, and genomic island prediction. Comparisons included 57 curated public L. interrogans genomes, including canine strains reported in association with severe and asymptomatic infections. Clinical, laboratory, and epidemiological records for the eight local cases were summarized descriptively. All eight isolates were classified as L. interrogans ST17, with identical allelic profiles and ANI values approaching 100%, indicating a highly conserved lineage despite variation in clinical signs and laboratory findings. Genomic conservation extended to virulome, the type I-C CRISPR-Cas system, the c-di-GMP signaling repertoire (37 proteins), and the overall distribution of genomic islands predominantly on chromosome I. The pangenome was open (~6800 gene families), but neither persistent-genome phylogeny nor the gene-content comparisons showed a consistent pattern separating the available genomes by reported clinical category in the analyzed dataset. These findings support the hypothesis that phenotypic variation may involve differential regulation of conserved genes, potentially through pathways such as c-di-GMP signaling, alongside host-related factors. Epigenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses, coupled with functional studies, are needed to test this hypothesis and elucidate the mechanisms underlying clinical heterogeneity.

title: Lipid nanoparticle-mediated RNA delivery enables protein expression in chicken testes.
authors: Jiang, Qi; Zhang, Haifeng; Rengaraj, Deivendran; He, Banghua; Wang, Mengqi; Huang, Yangtian; Yang, Xianguang; Li, Xin Zhiguo
abstract: RNA-lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are emerging tools for poultry vaccination, but methods for local protein expression in reproductive tissues remain underdeveloped. Here, we established RNA delivery to chicken testes using LNPs formulated with the ionizable lipid DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3) and multifocal intratesticular injection through an intercostal surgical approach. Bilateral injections were completed in all six chickens in a surgical-feasibility cohort, with postoperative recovery during the 7-day observation period. At an equal RNA mass dose of 80 microg per testis, conventional messenger RNA (mRNA) encoding enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) produced detectable reporter signals at days 1, 3, and 7, with the highest measured signal at day 3. An eGFP self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) construct showed delayed detectable expression at days 3 and 7. Delivery of mRNAs encoding CRISPR-associated protein 9 (Cas9) and the epitope-tagged recombination-related proteins DNA meiotic recombinase 1 (DMC1) and RAD51 recombinase (RAD51) also produced detectable proteins in testicular tissue. Following local delivery, testicular architecture was preserved, with minimal apoptosis and only a modest inflammatory response. These findings establish the feasibility of local RNA-LNP delivery for short-term protein production in chicken testes, providing a platform for future studies of male reproduction and genome editing.

title: Genome-wide identification of the EIN3/EIL gene family in potato and characterization of StEIN3/EIL2 in response to phosphorus starvation.
authors: Zhang, Feng; Xu, Xinlei; Cheng, Yingying; Yang, Junxi; Zhang, Haiyan; An, Yanlin
abstract: Phosphorus (P) is an essential macronutrient, and low inorganic phosphate (Pi) availability is a major constraint on potato (Solanum tuberosum) production. The ETHYLENE-INSENSITIVE3/EIN3-LIKE (EIN3/EIL) transcription factors integrate ethylene signaling with Pi starvation (low Pi) responses in model species, but this family has not been systematically characterized in potato. Here, nine StEIN3/EIL genes were identified in the potato genome; they are distributed unevenly across five chromosomes and appear to have expanded through tandem and segmental duplication. All members are intron-less and retain the conserved N-terminal EIN3 DNA-binding domain. Transcriptomic profiling and RT-qPCR analyses revealed divergent tissue-specific expression patterns, among which StEIN3/EIL2 was strongly and rapidly induced in roots by Pi deprivation and, together with StEIN3/EIL4 and StEIN3/EIL8, localized to the nucleus. CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of StEIN3/EIL2 compromised root growth and reduced soluble Pi accumulation specifically under low Pi, identifying StEIN3/EIL2 as a positive regulator of the Pi starvation response. StEIN3/EIL2 interacted with the promoter of the central Pi signaling regulator StPHR1 in a yeast one-hybrid assay and activated transcription from this promoter in a heterologous transient system, and knockout of StPHR1 abolished low Pi-induced root elongation and reduced Pi accumulation. These findings establish a StEIN3/EIL2-StPHR1 module that links ethylene signaling to Pi starvation adaptation in potato and provide candidate targets for breeding Pi-efficient cultivars.

title: OSTM1 restrains B-cell lymphomagenesis by promoting PDE3B degradation and activating cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling.
authors: Tariq, Muhammad Usama; Sheshadri, Namratha; Shen, Jianliang; Jung, Jaeyong; Li, Rongrong; Sajjad, Hassan; Koch, Mark C; Lu, Kevin; Yan, Junrong; Rosati, Barbara; Caso, Giuseppe; Vallat, Brinda; Burley, Stephen K; Wang, Jun; Glytsou, Christina; Sun, Yi; Liu, Tong; Li, Hong; Chen, Suzie; Yang, Jiekun; Shen, Zhiyuan; Lin, Richard Z; Hinrichs, Christian S; Bertoni, Francesco; Wang, Y Lynn; Vacher, Jean; Xie, Ping; Zong, Wei-Xing
abstract: Through a genome-wide forward CRISPR/Cas9 screen in interleukin-3 (IL3)-dependent Ba/F3 cells, we identified osteoclastogenesis-associated transmembrane protein 1 (OSTM1) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor. Analysis of patient datasets revealed that OSTM1 is frequently deleted or downregulated in human B-cell malignancies (BCM). In mice, Cd19-Cre-driven B cell-specific monoallelic or biallelic deletion of Ostm1 cooperated with Cdkn2a loss to drive lymphomagenesis with near-complete penetrance. Mechanistically, OSTM1 directly interacts with phosphodiesterase 3B (PDE3B) and promotes its proteasomal degradation. Because PDE3B hydrolyzes cyclic AMP (cAMP), loss of OSTM1 stabilizes PDE3B, leading to suppression of tumor-suppressive cAMP-dependent PKA/CREB signaling and promotion of oncogenic transformation. Consistent with this mechanism, PDE3B is frequently amplified or upregulated in BCM, and expression of CREB/CREBBP transcriptional targets correlates positively with OSTM1 expression but inversely with PDE3B across BCM cohorts. Importantly, silencing Pde3b reverses oncogenic transformation driven by Ostm1 loss. Together, these findings establish OSTM1 as a tumor suppressor and uncover an OSTM1/PDE3B/cAMP signaling axis that restrains B-cell lymphomagenesis and may represent a therapeutically actionable vulnerability.

title: Effect of Y1Ste20 gene knockout on the mycelial morphology of Chaetomium globosum CGMCC 6882.
authors: Wang, Zichao; Liu, Yongyong; Hu, Rongxuan; Guo, Yimiao; Wu, Han; Zhu, Danye; Wang, Qi; Qiao, Xueyi
abstract: Chaetomium globosum CGMCC 6882 is an endophytic fungus isolated from Gynostemma pentaphyllum. However, its mycelia tend to intertwine and aggregate during submerged fermentation, eventually forming dense mycelial pellets. This phenomenon severely impedes diffusion and transfer of oxygen and nutrients from the fermentation broth to the interior of the mycelial pellets, thereby limiting the fermentation efficiency of C. globosum CGMCC 6882. To address this issue, a recombinant plasmid, pFC332-5 SrRNA-Ste20 gRNA, targeting the Y1Ste20 gene was constructed using CRISPR-Cas9 genome-editing technology. Subsequently, a Y1Ste20 gene knockout mutant, designated C. globosum XY1104, was successfully obtained through protoplast transformation, regeneration, and screening and identification. Results from solid dishes and liquid culture media investigations showed that C. globosum XY1104 exhibited a significantly lower mycelial growth rate than the parental strain, C. globosum CGMCC 6882. Moreover, its mycelia were shorter and more slender, and exhibited a denser distribution, with the formation of mycelial pellets completely eliminated. These findings demonstrate that Y1Ste20 is a key functional gene involved in regulating mycelial growth and morphological development in C. globosum and that targeted modification of this gene can be used to achieve morphological modification of fungus. Overall, this study provides reference for morphological regulation of other filamentous fungi.

title: CRISPR/Cas9-based Targeting of MicroRNA and Protein-Coding Homologs (MIR160, MIR167, and CAMTA3) from B. juncea: Targetability assessment of sgRNAs and MIR160 functional studies in heterologous system of A. thaliana.
authors: Chattopadhyay, Swetannita; Yadav, Shobha; Singh, Swati; Singh, Anandita
abstract: CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing is a powerful tool for functional genomics in crops. However, targeting specific gene locus is challenging in polyploid B. juncea harbouring multiple gene homologs. Design of sgRNAs necessitates careful consideration for achieving target specificity while reducing off-targets. Herein, we present a systematic workflow that combines in-silico sgRNA prediction with in-vitro cleavage assays to pre-screen guide RNAs specific to B. juncea homologs. The guides targeting conserved regions of MIR160 were functionally validated in heterologous system of A. thaliana. Computationally predicted sgRNAs were in-vitro tested in non-coding MIR160 (14 copies), MIR167 (15 copies), and protein coding genes viz. CAMTA3 to demonstrate applicability in CRISPR/Cas9-based editing and transcriptional regulation experiments. Analysis of cleavage assays confirmed that both number and positional distribution of mismatches in the PAM proximal seed region affect Cas9 activity. In MIR160 and MIR167, several sgRNAs showed in-vitro cleavage activity across multiple homologs, suggesting suitability for multiplexed editing of homologous genes. Although, deactivated Cas9 is employed in CRISPR activation/ interference experiments, targetability of sgRNAs specific to CAMTA3 could be validated via in-vitro targetability assays containing active Cas9 instead of dCas9. Based on cleavage assays, polycistronic assembly of a minimum of 8, and, 5 sgRNAs is recommended for editing of 14 and 15 homologs of MIR160 and MIR167, respectively, in B. juncea. Varying the order of multiplexed sgRNAs is proposed as a strategy to achieve selective or redundant editing. Combinations of guides are proposed for achieving in-vivo excision of ~58 nt fragment from MIR160 precursor sequences. Targetability of 3 guides has been validated for both editing and transcriptional regulation of CAMTA3. In-vivo validation of sg160_1, designed to simultaneously target 13 MIR160 homologs in B. juncea, was confirmed by mutation spectrum analysis of CRISPR-edited A. thaliana. The Ath-MIR160b locus showed editing (T1 and T2 generations) corresponding to moderate to severe developmental defects. To conclude, we propose an integrated CRISPR/Cas9-based work-flow for selective as well as redundant editing of homologous gene copies in polyploid B. juncea, thereby facilitating deployment of CRISPR/Cas9 strategies for Brassica crop improvement.

title: Precision gene targeting: comparative roles of siRNA, miRNA, and CRISPR technologies in gene silencing and genome editing: a review.
authors: Aboelhassan, Dalia M; Abozaid, Hesham
abstract: Precision gene targeting has emerged as a powerful approach for selectively regulating gene expression and modifying disease-associated genetic pathways. Among the principal technologies, small interfering RNA (siRNA), microRNA (miRNA), CRISPR-Cas9, and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) provide distinct yet complementary strategies for gene regulation and genome manipulation. siRNAs mediate sequence-specific post-transcriptional gene silencing through degradation of complementary messenger RNA, enabling potent and generally transient suppression of target genes. In contrast, miRNAs are endogenous regulatory RNAs that modulate multiple transcripts through translational repression and mRNA destabilization, thereby influencing diverse cellular processes and regulatory networks. CRISPR-Cas9 expands the scope of precision gene targeting by enabling programmable modification of genomic DNA, whereas CRISPRi uses catalytically inactive Cas9 to achieve targeted transcriptional repression without introducing DNA double-strand breaks. This review provides a comparative and critical analysis of these technologies, emphasizing their molecular mechanisms, target recognition, specificity, delivery strategies, therapeutic applications, clinical development, advantages, limitations, and safety considerations. Collectively, these platforms have demonstrated therapeutic potential across a broad range of diseases, including cancer, genetic and metabolic disorders, cardiovascular and neurological diseases, infectious diseases, and ocular disorders. However, important barriers to clinical translation remain, including delivery limitations, molecular stability, target and off-target effects, immunogenicity, toxicity, genomic instability, and the need for precise and durable control of gene modulation. For CRISPR-based approaches, additional considerations include modality-specific genomic alterations, prolonged editor activity, and the ethical and regulatory implications of permanent genome modification. Continued advances in molecular engineering, delivery technologies, target-selection strategies, and platform optimization may improve the specificity, safety, durability, and therapeutic efficacy of these approaches and facilitate their responsible integration into precision medicine.

title: Functional Dissection of cis-Regulatory Elements Controlling the Rice Florigen Gene RFT1.
authors: Ding, Yifeng; Nishide, Noriko; Izawa, Takeshi
abstract: The florigen gene RFT1 plays a critical role in regulating flowering time under artificial long-day (LD) conditions and functions prior to another florigen gene, Hd3a, under natural conditions in temperate regions of rice cultivation. Thus, RFT1 is important for the adaptation of rice to temperate areas of Asia. Compared with Hd3a, RFT1 is less strongly repressed under LD conditions. However, the cis-regulatory mechanisms governing RFT1 expression remain poorly understood. Here, we generated a series of CRISPR-Cas9 deletion mutants spanning an approximately 10 kb noncoding region surrounding RFT1. Expression and heading-date analyses identified multiple functional cis-regulatory regions involved in RFT1 activation. Combined analyses using mutants of the upstream Ghd7 regulator and Ehd1-overexpressing lines demonstrated that these regions function downstream of Ehd1 and Ghd7. Further fine-scale deletion and transient reporter assays revealed the importance of two Ehd1-binding sites among many candidate sites. Our results support a multilayered cis-regulatory architecture at the RFT1 locus and suggest evolutionary divergence in the regulation of FT orthologs between rice and Arabidopsis, as canonical CORE and CCAAT motifs appear to play only limited roles in RFT1 regulation. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic basis for the quantitative tuning of flowering time in rice cultivated in temperate regions.

title: A nonsense variant in KCNH7 (c.1324 C>T) is associated with a variable phenotypic spectrum of epilepsy.
authors: Jing, Wenwen; Li, Xiaowan; Zhang, Jiahui; Feng, Sirong; Song, Yue; Jia, Ying; Xie, Li; Meng, Lingdi; Du, Xilong; Yang, Shuanghao; Gu, Weiyue; Chen, Qian; Wang, Guangfu; Wang, Yi; Qiao, Shupei; Zhang, Xue
abstract: KCNH7 is a voltage-gated potassium (K(+)) channel (Kv) that regulates membrane excitability and K(+) flux across tissues. Studies using mouse models have suggested that Kcnh7 may play an important role in epilepsy susceptibility and pathogenesis. However, clinical and experimental evidence implicating KCNH7 variants in human epilepsy, as well as the genotype-phenotype association, remains unclear. Here, we aimed to refine the clinical, genetic, and functional electrophysiological features of a p.R442* variant identified in three individuals to elucidate potential genotype-phenotype association that may guide anticipatory management. We generated Kcnh7 mutants​ using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing. Heterozygous mutants exhibited increased neuronal hyperexcitability and increased seizure susceptibility due to reduced Kcnh7-encoded protein levels. Functional analyses established the KCNH7 p.R442* variant as a loss-of-function allele, with haploinsufficiency identified as a primary pathogenic mechanism. Our results underscore the significance of functional characterization for the KCNH7 p.R442* variant within the context of clinical interpretation, although larger cohorts are required to further validate these observations.

title: Explainable machine learning-assisted exploration of chromatin dynamics reveals chromosome-specific response to serum starvation.
authors: Redchuk, Taras; Pennanen, Antti P; Jaalinoja, Harri; Natri, Olli; Paavolainen, Lassi; Vartiainen, Maria K
abstract: Chromatin is dynamic at all length scales, influencing chromatin-based processes, such as gene expression. Even large-scale reorganization of whole chromosome territories has been reported upon specific signals, but the lack of suitable methods has prevented analysis of the underlying dynamic processes. Here, we have used CRISPR-Sirius for time-lapse imaging of chromatin loci dynamics during serum starvation. We show that chromosome 1 loci move toward the nuclear envelope during the first hour of serum starvation in a chromosome-specific manner. Machine learning-assisted exploration of acquired multiparametric data combined with the Shapley values-based explanation approach allowed us to uncover the critical features that characterize chromatin dynamics during serum starvation. This analysis reveals that although serum starvation affects overall nuclear morphology and chromatin dynamics, chromosome 1 loci display a specific response that is characterized by maintenance of dynamics in a constrained environment, and long 'jumps' at the nuclear periphery. Interestingly, the two homologous chromosomes display differential behaviors, with the more peripheral homolog being more responsive to the signal than the internal one. Overall, the presented machine learning-assisted dataset exploration helps us navigate the multidimensional data to understand the underlying dynamic processes and can be applied to a wide variety of research questions in imaging and cell biology in general.

title: Marker-based CRISPR screens identify POU2F1 as a regulator of DLL3 and neuroendocrine identity in small cell lung cancer.
authors: Cunniff, Patrick J; Fitzpatrick, Connor; Bauer, Jack; Skopelitis, Damianos; Pal, Sujay; Shanley, Liam; Taneja, Kamil; Klingbeil, Olaf; Yoshimoto, Toyoki; Joshua-Tor, Leemor; Vakoc, Christopher R
abstract: Small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) often exhibit a neuroendocrine lineage identity marked by high expression of Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3). Because DLL3 shows minimal expression in normal adult tissues, it serves as an SCLC-selective tumor antigen and is the basis for clinically efficacious targeted therapies. Understanding the mechanisms that regulate DLL3 expression is therefore critical for advancing therapeutic strategies in this disease. Here, we performed transcription factor-focused and genome-wide CRISPR screens to identify regulators of DLL3 expression in SCLC. Both approaches converged on POU2F1 as a top activator of DLL3 in this tumor context. Despite its ubiquitous expression, we identify an SCLC-specific role for POU2F1 in activating DLL3 and a broader set of neuroendocrine lineage genes. Epigenomic analyses reveal tandem POU2F1-ASCL1 motifs within the DLL3 promoter that underlie the functional cooperativity between POU2F1 and the neuroendocrine master regulator ASCL1 for high-level DLL3 expression in SCLC. We provide evidence that tandem POU2F1-ASCL1 elements are part of a cis-regulatory code for the lung neuroendocrine cell fate. Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized transcriptional logic controlling DLL3 expression and establish POU2F1 as a context-specific regulator of neuroendocrine lineage in SCLC.

title: Obesity-associated DNMT downregulation is linked to DNA hypomethylation of oncogenic pathways in endometrioid endometrial cancer.
authors: Cingoz, Harun; Asif, Huma; Kim, J Julie
abstract: Obesity plays a crucial role in the development and prognosis of endometrial cancer (EC), yet the molecular mechanisms underlying this association remain incompletely understood. In this retrospective comparative study, we investigated obesity-associated DNA methylation alterations in endometrioid EC using data from 229 patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Patients were stratified by body mass index (BMI) (lean < 25; obese >/= 30). Differential methylation analysis using the limma framework (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05, |logFC| > 1) identified 311 differentially methylated CpG sites (DMCs), 71% of which were hypomethylated in tumors from obese patients. This hypomethylated profile was accompanied by significant downregulation of DNA methyltransferases DNMT1, DNMT3A, and DNMT3B. Stratification by DNMT expression revealed that DNMT3A- and DNMT3B-low tumors displayed the most extensive methylation changes. CRISPR/Cas9 mediated DNMT3A knockout (KO) in HEC1B generated 2,000 DMCs, including 37 shared with obesity associated alterations. Pathway enrichment demonstrated convergence on estrogen response, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, TGF-beta signaling, and IL-2/STAT5 signaling. INPP5F, a negative regulator of PI3K/AKT signaling implicated in insulin sensitivity, was hypomethylated at the gene body CpG shared between obese tumors and DNMT3A KO cells, showed reduced expression in tumors from obese patients, and was associated with decreased overall survival. These findings suggest that DNMT downregulation may contribute to obesity-associated epigenetic remodeling in EC and could identify candidate methylation-associated genes linking metabolic dysfunction to disease progression.

title: Molecular mechanisms of AcrVA-mediated Cas12a inhibition and their potential applications.
authors: Kang, Yong Jun; Park, Hyun Ho
abstract: CRISPR-Cas12a is widely used for genome editing because it is simple, efficient, and suitable for multiplex targeting. However, strong or prolonged Cas12a activity can increase unwanted cleavage at off-target sites. This problem is especially important when Cas12a is used in complex microbial communities, where unintended editing may affect non-target microorganisms or mobile genetic elements. Anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins are natural inhibitors of CRISPR-Cas systems. Acr proteins targeting type V-A CRISPR-Cas12a systems are called AcrV proteins. Recent structural and biochemical studies have shown that AcrVA proteins inhibit Cas12a through highly different mechanisms. AcrVA1 induces cleavage of Cas12a-bound crRNA. AcrVA2 recognizes the nascent Cas12a polypeptide and promotes translation-dependent degradation of cas12a mRNA. AcrVA3 directly cleaves double-stranded DNA and indirectly reduces Cas12a activity. AcrVA4 allosterically blocks target DNA binding, whereas AcrVA5-AcrVA8 inhibit Cas12a by acetylating important lysine residues. These studies provide a structural basis for using AcrVA proteins as potential Cas12a off-switches. Importantly, AcrV proteins may reduce off-target effects by limiting the strength and duration of Cas12a activity after sufficient on-target editing has occurred. In this mini review, we summarize the structural mechanisms of AcrVA proteins and critically discuss the evidence and experimental requirements for their potential use in controlled Cas12a-based microbial engineering.

title: Establishment of an electrochemical sensor for detection of Helicobacter pylori based on CRISPR/Cas12a trans-cleavage activity.
authors: You, Xiaojuan; Zhu, Rui; Wang, Liuxiang; Li, Shuang; Su, Yajing; Liu, Xiaojin; Jin, Cong; Lai, Zihan; Gong, Yuesheng; Li, Yongwei
abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is one of the main causes of gastritis and gastric ulcers. Therefore, early detection of H. pylori is of great significance for the primary prevention of gastric cancer. Taking advantage of the trans-cleavage ability of Cas effector proteins, we developed a novel CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated electrochemical sensor for the detection of the vacAs1 gene of H. pylori. In this system, gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) were first electrodeposited on the gold electrode, which not only served to immobilize nonspecific ssDNA but also improved the conductivity of the electrode, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of the sensor. By combining recombinase-assisted amplification (RAA) with the trans-cleavage activity of CRISPR/Cas12a, changes in the amount of ssDNA were induced, further altering electronic transfer on the electrode surface. The developed CRISPR/Cas12a-based electrochemical biosensor exhibited a wider detection range (5.4 x 10(-19)-5.4 x 10(-13) M) and a low detection limit (9.5 x 10(-20) M). Moreover, the biosensor showed good recovery for the detecting H. pylori in spiked stool and artificial saliva samples. In addition, the biosensor exhibited good specificity and stability, suggesting that it may serve as a potential tool for the rapid, stable, and efficient detecting of H. pylori.

title: SLC38A2-Driven Glutamine Metabolic Reprogramming Promotes Hypoxic Survival in Glioblastoma.
authors: Qi, Yanhua; Xia, Huize; Gao, Zijie; Li, Boyan; Pan, Ziwen; Feng, Bowen; Wang, Chuanzheng; Ma, Weiyang; Li, Ruochuan; Qiu, Jiawei; Han, Zhe; Chen, Zheyuan; Tang, Weijie; Wang, Qingtong; Wang, Daiyan; Hao, Leyang; Liu, Junzhi; Zhao, Rongrong; Zhao, Hongyu; Li, Gang; Xue, Hao
abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is highly refractory to standard therapies, including anti-angiogenic agents such as bevacizumab. While bevacizumab prunes tumor vasculature, it exacerbates intratumoral hypoxia, which drives a metabolically resilient phenotype that limits survival benefits. This study aimed to identify the metabolic dependencies underlying GBM adaptation to hypoxia and to evaluate whether targeting these dependencies could enhance the antitumor efficacy of bevacizumab. Methods: We analyzed the spatial distribution of key metabolites in GBM patients and orthotopic xenograft mouse models using magnetic resonance spectroscopy and chemical shift imaging. A dual-vector hypoxia fate-mapping system paired with an in vivo genome-wide clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-CRISPR-associated protein 9 (Cas9) knockout screen was employed to identify metabolic vulnerabilities within the hypoxic niche. Metabolic flux was analyzed utilizing (13)C(5)-labeled glutamine tracers. The molecular mechanisms governing solute carrier family 38 member 2 (SLC38A2) regulation were investigated using chromatin immunoprecipitation, cycloheximide chase assays, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and co-immunoprecipitation. The efficacy of targeting SLC38A2 was evaluated through structure-based virtual screening and in vivo orthotopic xenograft models treated concurrently with zonisamide and bevacizumab. Results: Imaging and tissue metabolite analyses revealed a spatial metabolic mismatch in the hypoxic tumor core, characterized by lactate accumulation alongside glutamine depletion. In vivo CRISPR-Cas9 screening identified SLC38A2 as an essential metabolic dependency for GBM cell survival under hypoxic stress. Under hypoxic conditions, hypoxia-inducible factor 1 alpha (HIF-1alpha) promoted SLC38A2 transcription, while elevated lactate stabilized the SLC38A2 protein through alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1)-mediated lactylation at Lys472. These changes were accompanied by increased glutamine uptake and glutathione biosynthesis, reduced reactive oxygen species levels, and decreased mitochondrial-fission-mediated apoptosis. Pharmacological screening identified the US Food and Drug Administration-approved, brain-penetrant anticonvulsant zonisamide as an inhibitor of SLC38A2. In orthotopic GBM xenograft models, combined treatment with zonisamide and bevacizumab markedly suppressed tumor growth compared with bevacizumab alone. Conclusions: This study defines a spatially organized lactate-glutamine metabolic axis essential for hypoxic adaptation in GBM. The dual transcriptional and posttranslational up-regulation of SLC38A2 represents a critical survival mechanism. This axis can be pharmacologically dismantled by zonisamide, offering a clinically actionable combinational strategy to overcome anti-angiogenic therapy resistance.

title: Engineering innate immunity: CRISPR-Cas9 MPO knockout in hematopoietic stem cells abolishes chlorination and PMA-induced NET formation while preserving non-oxidative effector functions.
authors: Baron, Szilvia; Colamartino, Aurelien B L; Shapiro, Jenny; Schary, Yeshai; Garcia, Zulema Romero; Kohn, Donald B; Kahana, Anat; Elhasid, Ronit; Shukrun, Rachel
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Myeloperoxidase (MPO) is a key neutrophil heme peroxidase that contributes to antimicrobial oxidative killing. Emerging evidence implicates MPO in diverse inflammatory disorders, including atherosclerosis, autoimmune diseases, and neurodegenerative diseases. Since inherited MPO-deficiency is typically compatible with preserved host defense, inhibition or genetic deletion of MPO represents a promising strategy to mitigate MPO-driven tissue injury. METHODS: Human HSPCs were edited using CRISPR-Cas9 to generate MPO-knockout (MPO-KO) neutrophils, followed by in vitro differentiation. We systematically evaluated canonical neutrophil effector functions to determine which of them require MPO. Additionally, RAG2-KO was generated and used as a control for knockout procedure. RESULTS: MPO-KO did not significantly impair major neutrophil effector functions, including neutrophil elastase activity, fMLP-induced NE and MMP9 degranulation, phagocytosis of E. coli and S. aureus bioparticles, and superoxide production. In contrast, MPO-dependent chlorination was abolished and PMA-induced neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) release was profoundly reduced in MPO-KO neutrophils, while RAG2-KO control cells retained all of these functions. CONCLUSION: This strategy may offer a durable means to attenuate MPO-driven inflammatory damage, warranting further preclinical evaluation in relevant disease models.

title: Dense Granule Protein DG9 of Cryptosporidium parvum Interacts With DG10 at the Dense Band.
authors: Xiao, Qianqian; Ye, Ying; Liang, Zining; Luo, Li; Xu, Rui; Li, Na; Feng, Yaoyu; Xiao, Lihua
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
abstract: Cryptosporidium parvum, a protozoan parasite, causes life-threatening diarrhea in young children and immunocompromised individuals. During host cell invasion and intracellular proliferation, C. parvum secretes rhoptry, dense granule (DG), and small granule (SG) proteins into the parasite-host interface. These secreted proteins facilitate the biogenesis of the parasitophorous vacuole (PV) enclosing the parasite and the feeder organelle and electron-dense band (DB) at the parasite-host interface. Nevertheless, the molecular compositions of these organelles are poorly defined. Here, we characterized the subcellular localization and functional role of cgd1_470, a highly polymorphic protein associated with host adaptation in the parasite. Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated endogenous tagging, we revealed that cgd1_470 is a novel DG protein, designated DG9. DG9 is secreted to the parasite-host interface during invasion and localizes to the DB after the PV formation. Deleting the dg9 gene did not significantly alter the in vitro growth or in vivo pathogenicity of a virulent C. parvum strain. Proteomic screening identified several putative DG9-interacting partners, including DG10 (cgd7_4280) and SG5 (cgd1_640), both of which display a similar interfacial localization. We validated the physical interaction between DG9 and DG10 using coimmunoprecipitation and colocalization analyses. Taken together, these findings suggest that DG9 and DG10 are interacting components of the DB at the parasite-host interface.

title: Navigating the Drought Tolerance-Yield Trade-Off in Triticeae Cereals: From Molecular Networks to Climate-Resilient Breeding.
authors: Xiong, Jiangyan; Meng, Rong; Xu, Yunfeng; Peng, Yue; Shen, Qiufang; Zhang, Xiaoqin; Xue, Dawei; Zhang, Guoping
abstract: Drought driven by climate change severely threatens food security, particularly for wheat and barley grown in water-limited regions. A major breeding challenge is the trade-off between drought tolerance and yield. This review synthesises current knowledge of drought adaptation mechanisms in Triticeae crops, focusing on the transcriptional cascades, ABA-centric hormonal signalling and posttranslational modifications (kinases, phosphatases and ubiquitination) that confer resilience while often constraining carbon allocation to developing grains. Recent genomic advances, including genome-wide association study (GWAS), multi-omics integration and single-cell RNA-transcriptomics, have uncovered a wealth of drought-associated loci, although their translational potential is limited by data heterogeneity, environmental dependency and a persistent gap between laboratory validation and field performance. Emerging breeding approaches, such as speed breeding, wild-allele introgression, multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenotyping are accelerating the development of climate-smart cultivars. Tissue-specific and inducible expression systems show early promise in uncoupling stress protection from growth penalties. Looking ahead, we propose that overcoming the yield-tolerance trade-off will require integrating synthetic biology, explainable AI, systematic exploration of novel variation and field phenomics coupled with digital twin modelling. Collectively, this review provides a strategic framework for engineering next-generation, climate-smart Triticeae cereals capable of maintaining productivity under intensifying drought conditions.

title: A Live-Attenuated DeltaNcROM6 Strain Induces Protective Immunity Against Neospora caninum Infection in Mice and Sheep.
authors: Chen, Sining; Yu, Qile; Du, Boya; Wang, Jixia; Zheng, Ming; Liu, Feixue; Zhang, Xu; Liu, Zhenzhen; Zheng, Yuan; Gong, Pengtao; Zhang, Nan; Zhang, Xichen; Li, Xin; Wang, Xiaocen; Li, Jianhua
abstract: Neospora caninum (N. caninum) is a protozoan parasite associated with bovine and sheep abortion and canine neurological disorders. However, effective treatments and vaccines for controlling neosporosis remain limited. Rhomboid (ROM) serine proteases mediate apicomplexan invasion, but their function in N. caninum remains unclear. Here, CRISPR-Cas9 was used to construct the NcROM6 gene knockout strain (DeltaNcROM6), whose phenotypic traits and potential as a live-attenuated vaccine were evaluated in mouse and sheep models. NcROM6 deficiency markedly impaired in vitro invasion, egress, and intracellular proliferation. All mice infected with 2.5 x 10(7) DeltaNcROM6 tachyzoites survived, with tissue parasite burdens reduced by 68.30%-100% and attenuated tissue lesions. Neither residual virulence nor vertical transmission was detected postimmunization with 5 x 10(6) DeltaNcROM6 tachyzoites, supporting vaccine biosafety. ∆NcROM6 elicited high titers of specific IgG2c, activated CD4(+) T cells, and induced a mixed Th1/Th2 immune response, encompassing both humoral and cellular immunity. Immunized mice exhibited 100% survival against both acute and chronic N. caninum infection, and an 86.12% reduction in brain cyst burden against chronic infection. In sheep, immunization with ∆NcROM6 elicited persistent and significantly elevated levels of cytokines against N. caninum, resulting in significantly reduced parasite burdens across multiple tissues, and substantially ameliorated tissue lesions. Collectively, DeltaNcROM6 provides reliable and effective protection against N. caninum infection in both mouse and sheep models, indicating it as a promising live-attenuated vaccine candidate for controlling neosporosis in livestock.

title: Mapping the NFYA 3'UTR landscape identifies alternative polyadenylation as a targetable vulnerability in prostate cancer.
authors: Pagani, Giulia; Casirati, Chiara; Pandini, Cecilia; Fornezza, Stefania; Priami, Chiara; Fois, Giulia; Bisi, Sara; Mironov, Aleksei; Cacioppo, Roberta; Manfrini, Nicola; Zavolan, Mihaela; Nicassio, Francesco; Migliaccio, Enrica; Gandellini, Paolo
journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alternative polyadenylation (APA) is increasingly recognized as a pervasive oncogenic mechanism that reshapes post-transcriptional gene regulation and promotes tumor aggressiveness. Whether APA contributes to the dysregulation of NFYA-encoding the regulatory subunit of the oncogenic transcription factor NF-Y-in prostate cancer (PCa) remains largely uncharacterized. METHODS: We interrogated bulk, single cell and 3'-end RNA-sequencing data from PCa cell lines and patient samples to re-annotate and quantify the usage of NFYA 3'UTRs. The functional consequences of APA were assessed using reporter assays. NFYA APA was experimentally reprogrammed using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion and antisense oligonucleotide (ASO)-based masking of polyadenylation signals, followed by in vitro and in vivo phenotypic analyses. RESULTS: Four functional NFYA 3'UTR isoforms were identified, with one predominantly used across cell lines and tissues. PCa displayed pervasive NFYA 3'UTR shortening, which correlated with tumor grade and metastatic disease, increased NF-YA protein abundance, and enhanced proliferation. 3'UTR lengthening was instead observed upon induction of cellular quiescence or after Enzalutamide treatment. Mechanistically, 3'UTR lengthening reduced NF-YA protein expression through decreased mRNA stability, impaired translation, and enhanced nuclear retention, rather than increased miRNA-mediated repression. Enforced NFYA 3'UTR lengthening in PCa cells via CRISPR/Cas9 or ASOs diminished NF-YA protein levels and suppressed aggressive tumor traits both in vitro and in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish NFYA APA as a critical determinant of NF-YA oncogenic output and downstream tumor-promoting programs, and as a previously unrecognized driver of PCa progression. Importantly, they provide proof-of-concept for gene-specific, APA-directed therapeutic strategies. ASO-mediated modulation of polyadenylation indeed emerges as a clinically translatable approach to fine-tune oncogene expression, thus opening new avenues for RNA-based precision interventions in aggressive PCa.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals ANAPC1 overexpression and a potential TEAD4-associated regulatory relationship in cholangiocarcinoma.
authors: Wu, Ke-Jun; Wang, Lei; Zhan, Yan-Ting; Tang, Yu-Lu; Li, Ming-Jie; Li, Qi; Tang, Huan-Huan; Xie, Ying-Yi; Li, Zong-Yu; Li, Jian-Jun; Chen, Gang; Chen, Si-Yan
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cholangiocarcinoma (CHOL) is a highly heterogeneous and aggressive malignancy that is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage because of the lack of early biomarkers, resulting in a poor prognosis. Although ANAPC1 overexpression has been reported in other cancers, its role and regulatory mechanisms in CHOL remain insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: To characterize ANAPC1 expression in CHOL, identify candidate upstream transcriptional regulators, and elucidate the associated functional programs and pathways. METHODS: Multi-omics profiling was integrated with in-house immunohistochemical validation. Differential expression analyses, CRISPR-based functional screening, transcription-factor prioritization, ChIP-seq with epigenomic annotation, gene set enrichment analysis, spatial transcriptomics, and single-cell RNA-seq were conducted to investigate ANAPC1-associated regulatory mechanisms in CHOL.Structural modeling of predicted TEAD4-DNA complexes was additionally performed to assess the structural compatibility between TEAD4 and candidate ANAPC1 promoter motifs. RESULTS: ANAPC1 was significantly overexpressed in CHOL at both the transcriptomic level (436 CHOL vs. 213 non-CHOL samples) and the protein level (66 CHOL vs. 99 non-CHOL tissues), with spatial enrichment in cholangiocytes. Public CRISPR dependency screening indicated that ANAPC1 loss was associated with reduced cellular fitness in several CHOL cell lines, including HUCCT1. Integrative analyses identified TEAD4 as a candidate upstream regulator of ANAPC1, and TEAD4 was upregulated in CHOL. Public ChIP-seq and epigenomic datasets across multiple cell lines, including HUCCT1, HepG2, BE2-C, and MDA-MB-231, suggested TEAD4 occupancy at the ANAPC1 locus, together with active chromatin features such as H3K27ac signals near the promoter region. Across several bulk transcriptomic datasets, TEAD4 and ANAPC1 showed positive expression associations of varying magnitude, whereas spatial transcriptomics indicated partially overlapping regional enrichment within malignant areas.Protein-DNA complex modeling of a predicted candidate TEAD4-ANAPC1 promoter DNA complex yielded an ipTM score of 0.71 and a pTM score of 0.62 for the top-ranked candidate promoter motif. GSEA identified positive enrichment of proliferation- and RNA-processing-related pathways and negative enrichment of several immune-related pathways within the ANAPC1-correlated transcriptomic profile. Single-cell analysis further localized ANAPC1 expression mainly to cholangiocytes and identified a statistically significant but extremely weak cell-level correlation with TEAD4. CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the hypothesis of a putative TEAD4-ANAPC1 regulatory relationship in CHOL based on integrative epigenomic, transcriptomic, spatial, and structural analyses. Direct experimental validation is required to determine whether TEAD4 functionally regulates ANAPC1 transcription in cholangiocarcinoma.

title: N-acetyltransferase 10 promotes glioblastoma radioresistance by suppressing immunogenic ferroptosis through N(4)-acetylcytidine of SLC7A11 mRNA.
authors: Hu, Shushu; Cheng, Jinmei; Liu, Yuan; Chen, Chen; Qiu, Rubin; Liu, Yantan; Zhang, Qinghua; Xie, Yuyin; Wan, Binlong; Tan, Peixin; Xie, Dehuan; Lei, Yuan; Luo, Haizhen; Feng, Wenqing; Deng, Yushi; Hua, Xin; Ren, Chen; Du, Shasha
journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy is the standard treatment for glioblastoma (GBM), but its efficacy is severely compromised by radioresistance. While aberrant RNA modifications contribute to radioresistance, specific epitranscriptomic vulnerabilities remain underexplored. METHODS: We integrated quantitative proteomics, N(4)-acetylcytidine RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (acRIP-seq), and CRISPR dependency screens to identify radioresistance drivers in GBM. Mechanisms were investigated through patient cohorts, the use of a catalytically inactive mutant (NAT10-G641E), RNA stability assays, and polysome profiling. Immunological and clinical translational effects were assessed via orthotopic mouse models and computational drug repurposing. RESULTS: We identified N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10), the RNA N(4)-acetylcytidine (ac4C) writer, as a core driver of GBM radioresistance and poor patient survival. Mechanistically, NAT10 deposits ac4C onto SLC7A11 mRNA, stabilizing its transcript and enhancing translational efficiency, thereby fortifying cellular antioxidant defenses and enabling GBM cells to evade radiation-induced ferroptosis. Furthermore, targeting NAT10 induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) and orchestrated a "cold-to-hot" tumor microenvironment transformation, characterized by robust CD8(+) T cell infiltration. To circumvent the toxicity of existing NAT10 inhibitors, we repurposed pemetrexed as a safe and effective alternative. Pemetrexed disrupted the NAT10/ac4C/SLC7A11 axis, yielding profound synergistic survival benefits when combined with radiotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: NAT10 promotes GBM radioresistance via ac4C-mediated stabilization of SLC7A11 and evasion of ferroptosis. Repurposing pemetrexed to inhibit NAT10 presents a promising strategy to sensitize refractory GBM to radiotherapy by simultaneously triggering ferroptosis and enhancing anti-tumor immunity.

title: Recent advances in therapeutic signaling pathways in polycystic kidney disease: insights from contemporary translational disease models- a narrative review.
authors: Kugita, Masanori; Yamaguchi, Tamio; Nagao, Shizuko
abstract: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) has undergone a major conceptual reappraisal over the past decade. Although PKD is fundamentally a monogenic disorder caused by mutations in PKD1, PKD2, PKHD1, and related genes, it is now increasingly recognized that disease progression is regulated by complex and interconnected signaling networks arising from coordinated dysregulation across multiple regulatory pathways. Advances in experimental models, multi-omics technologies, and cross-species approaches have revealed that cyst initiation and progression arise from convergent defects in mechanosensation, epithelial proliferation, metabolic reprogramming, innate immune activation, and fibrotic remodeling. In this Review, we synthesize insights from genetically engineered mouse models, naturally occurring rodent strains, CRISPR/Cas9-based large-animal systems, and human cell-derived spheroids and induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived kidney organoids. We highlight how conditional knockout platforms define the spatial and temporal origins of cystogenesis, whereas hypomorphic and allele-specific models clarify mutation- and dosage-dependent determinants of disease severity. These complementary systems connect upstream polycystin dysfunction to downstream therapeutic hubs, including vasopressin-cyclic AMP signaling, mTOR and AMPK pathways, Hippo-YAP/TAZ mechanotransduction, the cGAS-STING inflammatory axis, microRNA regulatory networks, and the gut-kidney axis. We further discuss how pathway-informed testing across model systems has accelerated the development of mechanism-based interventions, including vasopressin V2 receptor antagonists, nucleic acid-based microRNA therapeutics, metabolic modulators, kidney-targeted drug-delivery strategies, and rational combination therapies. Finally, we outline emerging directions for network-informed and stage-specific treatment strategies, emphasizing lineage-resolved targeting and translational validation in large-animal and human-derived platforms. This integrated framework provides a foundation for future therapies aimed at modifying the natural history of PKD.Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Comparison of interventional causal structure learning algorithms for gene regulatory network inference.
authors: Sprengel, Jan L; Velten, Britta
abstract: BACKGROUND: Causal structure learning offers a promising approach to studying gene regulation in cells, aiming to provide deeper mechanistic insights than purely association-based methods. Theoretical groundwork indicating that interventions improve identifiability of causal structure motivates the use of causal structure learning methods in scenarios with interventional information. RESULTS: This benchmark investigates the ability of existing causal structure learning algorithms to leverage the information revealed by targeted interventions to infer gene regulatory networks (GRNs). In this study synthetic single-cell perturbation data and experimental data from a clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screen are leveraged, and a suite of causal structure learning algorithms is evaluated on metrics tailored to synthetic ground truth and real biological data respectively. On synthetic data, accurate recovery of GRNs was achieved under favourable conditions: strong interventions, large sample sizes, and low measurement noise. For experimental data, no reliable ground truth is available, so inferred GRNs were assessed indirectly, using observed perturbation effects and curated regulatory annotations. Here, performance remained unreliable, with technical and biological noise and algorithmic scalability as limiting factors. This highlights a current gap between theoretical potential and practical application of causal structure learning for GRNs. CONCLUSIONS: The benchmark provides insight into algorithm strengths and limitations and offers groundwork for further methodological development. We also provide an accessible software package for applying modern causal structure learning to custom datasets and thereby foster future exploration of its potential.

title: A broadly applicable somatic embryogenesis platform accelerates regeneration and genetic transformation in elite alfalfa.
authors: Li, Min; Zhou, Ying; He, Mengyun; Zhang, Huanhuan; Wang, Youmei; Kong, Zhaosheng; Zhu, Huisen; Wu, Shenjie
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) is a globally important perennial forage crop, but molecular breeding is constrained by slow, genotype-dependent regeneration and transformation. This bottleneck is particularly pronounced in elite commercial cultivars, for which efficient protocols are scarce. A robust, broadly applicable regeneration platform is therefore essential for functional genomics, genome editing, and targeted improvement of agronomic traits. RESULTS: Using the elite cultivar 'Zhongmu No. 1', which has a high-quality reference genome, we systematically optimized explant type and stage-specific culture conditions across the entire regeneration pathway. Stem explants cultured on the optimized callus-induction medium CIM-MS1 showed markedly reduced browning, a 3.5-fold increase in callus induction, and callus formation 10-20 days earlier than under the reference condition, while maintaining stable embryogenic morphology. Transcriptome analysis of 15-day stem-derived calli associated this response with enhanced carbohydrate metabolism, cell-wall remodeling, and expression of embryogenesis-related regulators. Transfer of embryogenic calli to plant growth regulator-free N6 medium increased somatic embryo production by 1.3-fold and accelerated conversion to plantlets. Compared to a previously reported protocol, the integrated pipeline increased the frequency of transgene-positive plants 2.8-fold and shortened the transformation cycle by 2 to 3 months. The system supported both transgene overexpression and CRISPR/Cas9 editing and, importantly, enabled complete somatic embryo-mediated regeneration in all 25 tested cultivars from diverse geographic origins. CONCLUSIONS: We established an efficient, stage-integrated regeneration and transformation platform for elite alfalfa. Its novelty lies in combining axenic clonal explants, low-browning embryogenic callus induction, plant growth regulator-free somatic embryo development, and direct plantlet conversion into a single streamlined workflow. The broad regeneration response across 25 cultivars substantially extends the utility of the system beyond a single highly responsive genotype. This platform removes a major technical barrier to functional genomics and precision breeding in cultivated alfalfa.

title: Optimized methodology for CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene knockout in tetraploid potato: targeting StBEL5 as a case study.
authors: Zounkova, Andrea; Chirivi, Daniele; Pribylova, Adela; Martignago, Damiano; Myslivcova, Jitka; Masek, Tomas; Fischer, Lukas; Betti, Camilla; Fornara, Fabio; Maskova, Petra
journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 has emerged as a powerful tool for targeted genome editing in plants; however, its application in cultivated potato Solanum tuberosum ssp. tuberosum remains challenging due to its vegetative propagation and complex highly heterozygous tetraploid genome. Availability of whole-genome sequence data for the specific genotype is crucial to ensure complete knockout of all alleles of target genes while minimizing off-target mutations. In this study, using Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of cultivar Desiree, we established a methodology to achieve complete CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene knockout. We show that repeated de novo regeneration could improve editing efficiency by promoting emergence of new mutations. We also present effective strategies for detecting mutations in target genes that may lack clear phenotypic manifestations, applicable to polyploid and potentially mosaic material, and possibly transferable to other crops. Demonstrated through our case study on StBEL5 gene, we propose an optimized, step-by-step methodological guide covering the entire workflow. In addition, we provide a basic phenotypic characterization of S. tuberosum ssp. tuberosum cv. Desiree plants with complete knockout of the StBEL5 gene. StBEL5 is a transcription factor known as one of the key regulators driving tuber formation in S. tuberosum ssp. andigena. Under tested conditions, our mutants unexpectedly showed only slightly delayed onset of tuberization, but their overall tuber yields were comparable to those of wild-type plants. This indicates that in ssp. tuberosum (cv. Desiree), the StBEL5 role in regulating tuber development is less significant than in ssp. andigena.

title: Genomic characterization of Pediococcus acidilactici AB01 isolated from Algerian Targui camel milk: insights into safety, probiotic-associated traits, and functional potential.
authors: Belbeldi, Abdessalem; Belaouni, Hadj Ahmed; Amokrane, Serine; Mahrouk, Abdelkader; Amorim-Neto, Dionisio Pedro; Sant'Ana, Anderson S; Boughellout, Halima
abstract: Pediococcus acidilactici displays substantial strain-level variation, requiring genome-resolved evaluation of new food-associated isolates. This study characterized P. acidilactici AB01, isolated from raw milk of Algerian Targui camels, and used previously generated in vitro observations only to contextualize genomic predictions. Illumina sequencing yielded a 2,117,438-bp draft genome with 42.0% GC content, 36 contigs, and an N50 of 389,234 bp. BUSCO recovered 99.2% complete markers, whereas CheckM estimated 98.23% completeness and 2.43% contamination. ANIb values calculated with IPGA were 99.01% and 98.71% relative to the P. acidilactici type-strain deposits DSM 20,284(T) and JCM 8797(T), respectively; dDDH values of 91.2% supported species assignment. ResFinder detected no known acquired antimicrobial-resistance genes, and no virulence-factor match satisfied the predefined identity and reference-coverage criteria. CARD-RGI additionally identified three distant Strict homolog matches (sdrM-like, qacG-like, and alr/vanT-like), which were examined according to their sequence characteristics and genomic contexts. Functional annotation identified candidate genetic determinants potentially associated with stress responses, carbohydrate metabolism, and cell-surface interactions, together with a predicted Type II-A CRISPR-Cas locus containing 29 spacers with putative viral matches. Comparative analysis of 85 P. acidilactici genomes identified an open pan-genome comprising 5,485 clusters (Heaps-law gamma = 0.266). Seventy-seven candidate clusters occurred only in AB01 within this dataset, of which 67 remained after excluding clusters containing partial coding-sequence annotations. Overall, these findings highlight the genomic diversity of P. acidilactici and identify AB01 as a promising candidate requiring further in-depth experimental evaluation before its safety and probiotic, biopreservative, or functional potential can be established.

title: PARG inhibition elicits cytotoxicity by sequestering XRCC1 and other PAR-binding proteins into PAR-dependent nuclear condensates.
authors: Dumoulin, Isaac; Lee, Brian J; Zhang, Chuhan; Lin, Xiaohui; Wang, Yunyue; Han, Richard P; Verma, Priyanka; Zha, Shan
abstract: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relax chromatin and recruit DNA repair factors. PAR is normally short-lived and rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors target homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we find that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of multiple PAR-binding factors (XRCC1-LIG3/POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, PARG itself) but not HR-deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (nuclear NAD(+) synthesis), or UNG confers resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces reversible PARP1- and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates in undamaged cells. While lacking detectable DNA breaks, these condensates sequester various PAR-binding proteins (e.g. XRCC1, ALC1, FUS), reducing their nuclear availability and impairing recruitment to bona fide DNA lesions. These findings identify PAR-binding protein sequestration as the mechanism underlying PARGi cytotoxicity, explain the paradoxical essentiality of PARG but not PARP1, and establish PAR-binding factor deficiency as a biomarker for PARGi.

title: Chromatin Remodeling of RasGRP3 Underlies Temozolomide Sensitivity in Glioblastoma Organoids.
authors: Chen, Bohan; Su, Guangsong; Huang, Yiting; Liu, Rong; Song, Yingjie; Xiao, Qian; Lian, Jie; Zhang, Chen; Qiu, Yuhan; Zhao, Qianlan; Gu, Jiayu; Zhong, Jian; Gao, Yixin; Wu, Xujia; Ma, Yiping; Zheng, Yaoqiang; Zhang, Meng; He, Anshun; Bi, Jinfang; Li, Peng; Zhao, Zhongfang; Shi, Jiandang; Zhang, Lei; Huang, Bin; Lu, Wange; Zhang, Nu
abstract: Acquired resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) constitutes a formidable clinical barrier in the management of glioblastoma (GBM). GBM organoid models (GBO) that faithfully mirror the parental tumor phenotype serve as powerful research instruments to overcome the limitations in this field. We established GBOs derived from primary glioma patients and their TMZ low-sensitivity counterparts. To unravel the intricate molecular underpinnings of this process, we performed an unbiased, integrated multi-omics analysis encompassing epigenomic, 3D genomic, and transcriptomic profiling, coupled with dual CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screening of TMZ-induced enhancers (TiEns) and their cognate target genes. Our findings demonstrate that enhancer-mediated 3D chromatin remodeling drives chemosensitivity predominantly by transcriptionally activating drug-sensitivity-associated genes, such as RasGRP3, VEGFA, BTN3A2, etc. Knockdown or knockout of these genes and enhancers renders glioma cells more sensitive to TMZ, especially RasGRP3. Our work unveils a druggable "enhancer-chromatin-target" signaling axis and proposes a novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy to surmount TMZ low sensitivity in GBM.

title: Integrated AI surveillance of wastewater: One health approach for pathogen detection and cancer risk assessment.
authors: Paul, Sonali; Rath, Debapriyo; Dutta, Rajdeep; Dutta, Sagnik; Mukherjee, Susmita
journal: Progress in molecular biology and translational science
abstract: Wastewater becomes one of the important pools for Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) and on fmicrobial signatures, representing the health status of the population at large using the One Health approach. This study suggests an integrated methodology applying shotgun metagenomics, machine learning algorithms, and biosensor technology in order to tackle the problem of diagnostic latency inherent in existing approaches to the assessment of the threat. With the help of genome-resolved metagenomics, the resistome of the wastewater is being characterized, focusing on the characterization of the -lactamases and mobile genetic elements responsible for the horizontal gene transfer process. In addition, the study analyzes the presence of biofilm-associated factors as well as virulence factors associated with carcinogenesis and represented by the pks genomic island in E. coli and the FadA protein in F. nucleatum. Machine learning algorithm architecture is used for the analysis of the network in order to determine the correlations between changes in the microbial community and emerging public health challenges. Moreover, CRISPR-based and electrochemical biosensors are being designed for the rapid and deployable surveillance in the field. Here is the full guide to what one found throughout our research- brilliant-salmon-gjvlohlav5.edgeone.app.

title: A Point-of-Care Integrated Detection System for Rapid Mycobacterium leprae Detection Using RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a and Lateral Flow Assay.
authors: Jiang, Haiqin; Wen, Bin; Shi, Ying; Zhang, Wenyue; Bai, Yuefan; Wei, Dongkai; Sapkota, Pradip; Yang, Heng; Wang, Hongsheng
journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Leprosy remains a significant public health challenge in many regions, and inadequate point-of-care (POC) diagnostics often delay treatment and lead to disability. We aimed to establish an optimized RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a POC system for M. leprae detection with integrated reagents, equipment and colloidal gold visualization. METHODS: The workflow comprised 1 min of tissue DNA release, 15 min of incubation and amplification in the instrument, and approximately 16 min for CRISPR detection. Assay conditions were optimized (200 nM primers, 37 degrees C, 100 nM each of Cas12a and crRNA), and analytical sensitivity and specificity against non-leprosy mycobacteria were evaluated. Clinical performance was assessed in 219 clinical samples and compared with Ziehl-Neelsen staining and PCR. RESULTS: The detection limit was 100 copy/muL for M. leprae DNA, with no cross-reactivity with other mycobacteria. Among 179 confirmed leprosy samples, CRISPR-Cas12a detected all multibacillary (MB) samples (100%) and 65.21% of paucibacillary (PB) cases, outperforming PCR (39.13%) and acid-fast staining (0%) and comparable to qPCR (63.04%). All non-leprosy samples were negative by CRISPR-Cas12a. CONCLUSIONS: This POC-compatible platform holds promise for early diagnosis, and the integrated reagents and equipment further enhance convenience for on-site testing in resource-limited settings, supporting timely intervention and leprosy control efforts.

title: Functional Loss of Invasion Quantified in a CRISPR Knockout Hydrogel Model.
authors: Skirzynska, Arianna; MacLeod, Graham; Angers, Stephane; Shoichet, Molly S
abstract: Genetic screens have transformed functional genomics but remain poorly suited for interrogating invasion phenotypes in defined three-dimensional (3D) microenvironments due to low nucleofection efficiencies and the lack of high-content, quantifiable invasion assays. Here we present a chemically defined hyaluronan-based hydrogel platform that enables quantitative, single-cell-resolved measurement of cell invasion and is compatible with arrayed CRISPR-Cas9 perturbation. Specifically, hyaluronan-oxime (HAox) was used to study the invasion of multiple patient-derived cell lines, modelling the invasive properties in two diseases - glioblastoma and lymphangioleiomyomatosis. Efficient CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of 93 genes allowed identification of potential invasion-suppressing targets, including effects detectable only at single-cell resolution. This framework expands functional genetic screening to complex invasion behaviours in controlled 3D microenvironments and may be broadly applicable to other heterogeneous disease models. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Cellular invasion in cancer drives tumour recurrence and metastasis. Identification of target genes which correspond to a quantitative functional loss of invasion is challenging due to the lack of physiologically relevant microenvironments to model cell invasion in vitro, and robust nucleofection protocols to efficiently knock out target genes. We report HAox, a hyaluronan-based hydrogel platform, designed based on components enriched in the diseased cell microenvironment. HAox can robustly identify invasiveness of diseased cells compared to healthy controls in two model diseases characterized by diffuse cellular invasion. HAox, coupled with efficient electroporation protocols to perform targeted gene knockout, enabled efficient knockout of 93 genes and quantification of cellular invasion, providing a platform for researchers to perform high-content screening against invasion phenotypes.

title: Lipid nanoparticles and their successors: Design principles for dense tissue penetration and clinical translation.
authors: Sands, Ian; du Moulin, Gary C; Giblin, Joshua; Chung, Eunji; Pickett, Maddie; Yau, Anne; Snow, Mari Anne; Chen, Yupeng
abstract: Nucleic acid therapeutics have transformed modern medicine, enabling targeted treatments that address a wide range of diseases at their genetic roots. From RNAi-mediated gene silencing to mRNA vaccines and CRISPR-based editing, these advances offer precision strategies for previously intractable conditions. The success of these modalities hinges entirely on delivery technologies which have evolved lockstep with nucleic acid research, facilitating transport from administration site to intracellular target(s). Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the leading delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics which is partially due to extensive research and development of lipid-based vehicle derivatives previously developed for small molecule-based drugs. While LNPs themselves have a relatively brief clinical history, the COVID-19 pandemic propelled nucleic acid technologies into the global spotlight, accelerating public, industrial, and regulatory engagement. This surge in attention catalyzed the maturation of clinical, manufacturing, and regulatory frameworks for therapies that rely on delivery technologies like LNPs for success. While this progress has enabled a new wave of therapies, it has also underscored the limitations of LNPs, including poor penetration into dense extracellular matrix (ECM) tissues and dose-limiting toxicities driven by immunogenicity. As optimization of LNP formulations continues, a new generation of nanoparticle platforms is emerging, aiming to address these shortcomings in morphology, chemistry, and tissue specificity. These platforms are well-positioned to leverage the translational groundwork laid by LNPs, potentially accelerating their own path to clinical relevance. In this review, we examine the evolution and clinical impact of LNPs, analyze their key limitations, and explore emerging delivery platforms, such as biomimetic nanoparticles and polymeric systems that seek to overcome the physicochemical limitations of LNPs while building on the lessons and regulatory frameworks they established.

title: A Cas9(D10A) nickase mouse line for precise genome editing.
authors: Trombke, Janine; Bauersachs, Daniel; Diaz, Carlota Farre; Rajewsky, Klaus; Chu, Van Trung; Kuhn, Ralf
abstract: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene editing involves DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) whose repair can generate unintended on- and off-target mutations. Here, we report a transgenic mouse line ubiquitously expressing Cas9(D10A) nickase, which creates targeted single-strand breaks (SSBs) to stimulate precise gene editing while substantially reducing the undesired editing products associated with Cas9 nuclease. We demonstrate the versatility of this resource in primary T cells, B cells, and hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), achieving efficient (5%-50%) high-fidelity reporter integration and introduction of cancer-relevant mutations at the Cd79b and Notch1 loci. By enabling precise, low-mutation-burden gene editing directly in primary cells, the Cas9(D10A) nickase mouse line provides a resource for inserting mutations relevant for hematopoietic disorders and malignancies and may be utilized more broadly for precision genome engineering across primary cell types.

title: Heat stress impairs pharyngeal tooth mineralization via TRPV1 in zebrafish.
authors: Ren, Yujia; Liu, Jingyun; Wang, Zhen; Fu, Jing; Zheng, Huiwen; Xing, Xianghui
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature is a fundamental environmental factor that governs a wide range of biological processes in ectotherms. Heat stress is known to disrupt development, yet its impact on specific physiological processes such as tooth biomineralization, and the underlying molecular thermosensing mechanisms, remain poorly understood. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether elevated temperature impairs pharyngeal mineralization in zebrafish and if so, whether the thermosensitive TRPV1 channel mediates this effect. METHODS: Zebrafish larvae were reared at 28  degrees C, 30  degrees C, 32  degrees C or 34  degrees C for 20 days. Pharyngeal tooth mineralization was assessed by Alizarin Red S staining and scanning electron microscopy. Expression of mineralization-related genes (odam, scpp5, scpp1, scpp9) was quantified by qRT-PCR. Tissue morphology was examined by HE staining. TRPV1 involvement was tested by pharmacological inhibition (AMG517) and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated trpv1 knockdown. RESULTS: Higher temperatures progressively impaired tooth mineralization, with patchy staining, changes in ameloblast-like cell morphology, and rough, pitted enameloid surfaces, despite normal survival and morphology. Gene expression of odam, scpp5, scpp1 and scpp9 was consistently downregulated. Both TRPV1 inhibition and trpv1 knockdown substantially rescued the heat-induced defects, restoring mineralization, surface structure and gene expression without affecting viability. CONCLUSION: Heat stress disrupts pharyngeal tooth biomineralization in zebrafish via TRPV1. TRPV1 is essential for this effect, positioning it as a key molecular link between environmental temperature and tooth formation.

title: CRISPR/Cas for diatom gene editing: pitfalls, solutions, and emerging tools.
authors: Sekulic, Mirna; Cleyman, Arthur; Vyverman, Wim; De Veylder, Lieven
abstract: Diatoms are ecologically important unicellular photosynthetic microalgae that are of increasing interest in biotechnology. Remarkably, probably due to their complex evolutionary history, diatoms hold many species-specific genes, most of which have an unknown function. The development of CRISPR/Cas-based genome editing techniques offers a unique opportunity to elucidate the function of these genes and to introduce novel traits of interest. Just as Arabidopsis thaliana serves as the reference model for higher plant genetics, Phaeodactylum tricornutum has emerged as the principal model for diatom genome editing. Its CRISPR/Cas toolkit comprises Cas9, Cas12a, CRISPR interference, and genome-wide screens. However, progress remains uneven. Methods optimized for P. tricornutum are not readily transferable to other diatoms, which often require species-specific adjustments. In this review, we discuss the current state of CRISPR/Cas-mediated editing in diatoms and, where relevant, compare it with the more well-established field of plant genome editing. We argue that extending these tools is essential to understand diatom biology and realize their full biotechnological potential.

title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment.
authors: Wang, Shiting; Qian, Qiheng; Liu, Yuting; Ding, Yang; Yang, Dechang; Zheng, Xing; Cheng, Sijin; Huang, Guoquan; Gao, Ge; Xiao, Jingfa; Zhang, Zhang; Jiang, Shuai
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition-associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type-specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type-enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

title: Targeting cancer immune evasion with anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate potentiates anti-PD-1 efficacy in colorectal cancer.
authors: Chen, Siqi; Liu, Qishan; Ye, Shubiao; Yu, Jing; Xie, Yongxin; Yuan, Yuhai; Song, Jianning; Du, Yaqing; Li, Min; Zhang, Xueli; Ma, Yanping; Lin, Zhensen; Zhang, Yu; Guan, Xin-Yuan; He, Guiwei; Jiang, Chen; Fang, Xiaona; He, Xiaosheng; Li, Lei; Lan, Ping; Yan, Qian
abstract: Loss of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) antigen presentation in tumor cells drives immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in colorectal cancer (CRC). To identify therapeutic targets reversing this, we conducted fluorescence-activated cell sorting-based CRISPR activation screens using a druggable genome library and identified folate receptor alpha (FOLR1) as a top negative regulator. FOLR1 was heterogeneously expressed in CRC tumors but undetectable in adjacent normal tissues. High expression of FOLR1 predicted a poor ICB response, enhanced cancer stemness, and unfavorable patient outcomes. Functional assays showed that FOLR1 promoted CRC stemness-associated properties and fostered an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) with impaired CD8(+) T cell infiltration and cytotoxicity, thereby driving tumor progression. Proteomic analyses revealed that FOLR1 stabilized the lactyltransferase AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1), which lactylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) at lysine-193 (K193), facilitating its interaction with TCPTP (T cell protein-tyrosine phosphatase) and inducing STAT1 dephosphorylation at tyrosine-701. Consequently, impaired STAT1 signaling down-regulated MHC-I and up-regulated MYC proto-oncogene protein (c-MYC), facilitating evasion of T cell surveillance and enhancing cancer stemness. The anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) mirvetuximab soravtansine (IMGN853) exhibited potent activity against FOLR1-positive CRC cells, reprogramming the TME to an immune-active status. Combining IMGN853 with anti-PD-1 (programmed cell death protein-1) therapy boosted antitumor immunity, sensitized tumors to immunotherapy, and induced robust tumor regression in vivo.
